newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian airport to pay its first ever dividend.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian airport to pay its first ever dividend.

text.p: Slovenia's main airport, unlisted Aerodrom Ljubljana, said on Tuesday it has decided to pay its first ever dividend this year.
"The dividend will be 65 tolars ($0.4) per share and will be paid from unpaid profits for the years 1993, 1994, 1995 and 1996," the company's chief executive Vinko Moze told Reuters.
The company's 1996 profit rose 33 percent to 278.4 million tolars ($1.75 million), while sales in the same period were up to 3.3 billion tolars from 2.9 billion.
In 1996 the airport invested 329.5 million tolars ($2.01 million), mainly on construction and new equipment.

The company said it planned to invest 26 million marks ($14.8 million) on infrastructure and security systems and some eight million marks on the development and maintenance of information systems until the year 2000.
The state owns 55.69 percent of the airport and the rest is held Slovenian institutional and retail investors. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
